_comment: Advisories with no fix that is not a framework major or a beta release.
Each entry needs a reason and a review date. scripts/audit-gate.js fails
the build on anything not listed here, so this file is the whole
argument for shipping with a known advisory - not a place to park work.

allowed.@auth/core: Critical: email normalizer validates before Unicode normalization, allowing a homoglyph @ bypass. Advisory range is *, so no released version is unaffected and there is nothing to upgrade to. Reachable only via the Email provider, which this app does not use: app/lib/auth.js runs Credentials plus OAuth. Revisit when Auth.js ships a fixed line.
allowed.next-auth: Same advisory, inherited from @auth/core. npm offers 4.24.7 as the fix, which is a DOWNGRADE from the installed 4.24.15 and forfeits every patch since. Real fix is next-auth v5, still beta.
allowed.postcss: Reached only through next's build toolchain, so it goes with the next major above. Not part of the served runtime.
allowed.nodemailer: High: a message-level `raw` option bypasses disableFileAccess/disableUrlAccess. app/lib/email.js never passes `raw` - it sends from/to/subject/html/attachments/headers and nothing else. Upgrading to 9.x also breaks next-auth, which declares nodemailer ^7.0.7; npm marks the tree invalid. Breaking auth is worse than an advisory we do not trigger.
allowed.next: High: DoS via the Image Optimizer on self-hosted deployments. Fix is next 16, two majors from the 14.2 line this app is built on. That is a migration, not a launch-week patch.
